correctness.rationale: For a,b odd and c even, f(x) has simple roots of opposite parity modulo 2; Hensel factorization shows the adjacent valuation pair reduces on the two parities to two-centre collisions with depths 1 and d. The discriminant identity gives d exactly. A two-centre ultrametric lemma supplies every single residue cell and the exact discrepancy; geometric valuation tails justify convergence of second moments and covariance. Tests of 128 coefficient triples against 81 cells and modular residue classes passed. Assumptions exclude zero observed values; no finite test substitutes for the argument.

value.rationale: The joint law is a complete two-point invariant for an infinite natural family of quadratic valuation trees; the universal one-class cell property, parameterized forbidden pairs, all realizable covariance values, and sharp sign boundary R≡8 mod16 versus 16|R provide structural information absent from one-point classifications. The excluded dyadic case of the related odd-prime root-collision method is mathematically meaningful due to its forced parity collision depths, not an arbitrary slice.
